automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.policy: Include only public web sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to the run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, stale, secondary-only, broad-upstream-only, and lower-boundary date-only candidates.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds model defaults and MCP startup controls
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub reported that Copilot for JetBrains gained enterprise-managed default model settings, a setting to disable automatic MCP server startup for Copilot and Claude, diagnostic-to-fix actions, clearer account and conversation controls, and reliability fixes across agent sessions, customizations, and worktrees.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: agent instructions should treat default model choice, MCP startup, diagnostic repair actions, and worktree reliability as governed environment configuration rather than ad hoc prompt content.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Do not create local product or MCP encyclopedia coverage; preserve only the downstream governance, instruction, and agent-workflow implications.

qualifying_updates.title: Octomind compares MCP, CLI, and skills by context cost and capability shape
qualifying_updates.summary: Octomind measured 14 tools across three MCP servers at 7,553 schema tokens before any prompt and argued that CLI commands fit stateless familiar tools, MCP fits stateful tools or credentialed structured results, and skills teach when and how to use those capabilities. The post recommends on-demand capability loading, caps on active capabilities, and measured tool-schema budgets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: governed tool design should budget context, avoid eager schema loading, keep credentialed/stateful operations behind capability boundaries, and treat skills as activation knowledge rather than a replacement for typed tools.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Upstream owns product, company, and protocol background. Local coverage should retain only practice guidance around context budgets, capability loading, credentials, and tool-selection criteria.

qualifying_updates.title: Octomind frames open-weight coding models as repo-level evaluation and licensing decisions
qualifying_updates.summary: Octomind reported real-pull-request benchmark results for open-weight coding models, contrasted open weight with open source, and emphasized that license terms, checkpoint availability, serving requirements, and behavior audits affect whether a team can keep operating the evaluated workflow.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: model selection for coding agents should record license terms, benchmark task provenance, cost, operational serving constraints, and retest triggers instead of treating leaderboard rank as a durable workflow decision.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Broad model, company, license, and benchmark facts route upstream; the local note is the eval/governance practice for reproducible agent model selection.

qualifying_updates.title: Chris Pietschmann argues production AI code still needs human-owned review gates
qualifying_updates.summary: The post recommends competent human review for production-bound AI-generated changes, bounded repair loops, protected checks and policies, scrutiny of dependencies and lockfile changes, branch protections, and traceability from approved revision to tested deployed artifact.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: AI-assisted development workflows should separate generated implementation speed from assurance ownership, and should place gates, approvals, dependencies, package-install review, and provenance outside the agent's unilateral control.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: No local entity leaf needed; this is a downstream coding-practice and governance source.

qualifying_updates.title: Boundev proposes a rubric for grading AI-generated code
qualifying_updates.summary: Boundev recommends small, anchored rubrics for AI-generated code, with criteria such as correctness against the brief, security, maintainability, scope discipline, and test quality. It recommends written rationales and inter-rater agreement checks before relying on rubric scores or LLM judges.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: coding-agent evals should preserve human-scored calibration sets, rationale text, scope-discipline checks, and security gates rather than collapsing generated-code quality into pass/fail tests.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Benchmark and organization facts are upstream-owned; retain the local rubric/eval design implications.

qualifying_updates.title: iTechGuides describes risk-focused review of AI-agent pull requests
qualifying_updates.summary: iTechGuides recommends treating an AI agent's summary as a claim, starting review from the requested outcome, checking repository, PR title, author and branch, inspecting the patch and surrounding code, prioritizing security-sensitive paths, and verifying claims against code and tests before a named human approves the change.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice implication: AI-assisted review workflows should preserve request-to-diff traceability, verify agent claims at source locations, and record human approval against the actual patch under review.
qualifying_updates.routing_note: Keep product-specific Codex background upstream; local use is a source-workflow and code-review practice note.
